answer: The protocol mandates 3,000 units of memory-hard work per session to gate access, where a verifier treats each agent as a unique vertex within a graph of active service commitments. An honest participant pays for one unit of compute, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, revealing overlaps in the orchard of concurrent tasks.
